text: Mark Haddon's The Curious Incident of the Dog in the Night-Time was removed from the Lake Fenton, Mich. summer reading program in 2010 after parents complained about its "foul language". The Wilson County School Board in Tennessee voted to remove it from the school system's approved reading list over its use of the F-bomb, then overturned the ban. In the Westmont (PA) Hilltop School District, complaints about "foul language", "profane use of God's name" and a "negative portrayal of a character with autism or a similar disorder" led a curriculum committee to recommend leaving the book off the voluntary summer reading list. Olentangy Ohio District Superintendent Scott Davis, acting on a parent's complaints, removed it from Liberty High School's optional summer reading list.
meta_description: The Curious Incident of the Dog in the Night-Time by Mark Haddon: removed from reading lists in Michigan, Tennessee and Ohio; recommended off one in Pennsylvania.
